citation: Oyake K, Murayama J, Tateishi T, Mochida A, Matsumoto M, Tsujikawa M, et al. Comparison of the sit-up test and head-up tilt test for assessing blood pressure and hemodynamic responses in healthy young individuals. Blood Press Monit. 2021;27(2):79-86.
protocol: Sit-up test and 70-degree head-up tilt in random order, 10 min apart. 10 min supine rest on the tilt table before each test; supine values are the mean of the final 2 min of that rest. Sit-up: passive move to sitting within 30 s, held 3 min. Tilt: elevated to 70 degrees over about 30 s, held 3 min. Sampling is beat-to-beat (Finapres); the supine block is the baseline.
population: 19 analysed (21 recruited, 2 lost to technical failure): 9 male, age 24.3 +/- 2.4 y, BMI 20.9 +/- 1.8; healthy adult volunteers aged 20-40, no underlying disease, no history of syncope.
note: Table 1 prints a supine column for each test (same people, order randomised), mean +/- SD per footnote; read the supine rows only, since the upright rows are not usable here. The 10-min rest and final-2-min averaging are in Methods, not in the table.
